contrary_evidence: The France PMI reading is a survey measure and not official output or GDP; the report states this limitation.
Euro-zone aggregate PMI remains above 50 at 51.7 while France is at 46.2 and Germany at 55.0, demonstrating divergence rather than a uniform European contraction.
Chinese iron-ore imports and crude-steel output are not directly comparable measures because ore grades, domestic ore, stock changes and shipment timing affect the relationship.
The IEA reports a recovery in global crude supply and higher observed stocks, while on-land stocks remain low and diesel prices remain above pre-war levels.
The Brazil unit export value is derived from value divided by net mass, not a quoted benchmark price.
limitations: The SteelHome inventory survey is not a complete official census and trader-held inventory is estimated.
The iron-ore import and steel-output series use different definitions and cannot establish a direct one-for-one demand relationship.
The Brazil Comex Stat NCM 2601 extraction is not preserved as a direct query/export artifact; the revision records flow, period, NCM, measures and formula.
SimFer progress and shipment figures are company disclosures, not independent operating audits.
The ECB credit-risk discussion is qualitative; no comparable same-day global credit-spread series is included.
The conflict discussion is attributed to IEA and Reuters; the report does not assign responsibility for every individual maritime incident.
